# FTI Studio


> Free, lightweight, single-purpose Windows desktop image editor built for ultra-fast, single-image touch-ups and digital art.


Launched on August 5, 2026, FTI Studio is an intentional, minimal utility designed to eliminate the startup friction and heavy memory footprint of complex suites like Photoshop for trivial edits.


## Metadata
- **Type**: Desktop Application
- **Platform**: Windows only
- **Cost**: 100% Free (No accounts, no subscriptions, no premium tiers, works completely offline)
- **Target Audience**: Casual users, digital artists, and anyone needing zero-friction, one-image quick fixes.


## Technical Specifications & Performance
- **Startup Time**: Under 1 second (on modern hardware)
- **Memory Footprint**: Under 30 MB RAM
- **Undo/Redo Depth**: Strictly 1 single step back (destructive editing workflow)
- **Layer Support**: None (flat canvas only)


## Core Capabilities
- **Editing Tools**: Draw tool, Erase tool, Color picker, and Resize tool (accessed via `File > Canvas Size`).
- **Best For**: Cropping, removing watermarks, making minor image corrections, and drawing/digital art.


## File Format Support
- **Native Format**: `.fti` (Flat Transparency Image). Note that exporting to `.fti` may alter file sizes depending on color complexity (e.g., a 1 MB PNG may become 4 MB, whereas a 42 KB file may drop to 40 KB).
- **Import/Export**: Exclusively supports PNG files via `File > Open (PNG)...` and exports back to PNG.
- **Unsupported Formats**: Does NOT natively support JPEG, GIF, BMP, or any other standard formats. External conversion to PNG is required prior to import.
- **Name Coincidence**: Has absolutely no relation to FamiTracker or FamiTracker Instrument (`.fti`) files; it has zero audio capabilities.


## Strategic Comparison Context
- **vs. Paint.NET**: Paint.NET offers full undo history, multi-format support, and layers, but has higher memory usage (~150 MB) and a 2–3 second boot time.
- **vs. Affinity Photo**: Affinity Photo provides a professional, cross-platform, non-destructive design toolkit, but demands 300+ MB RAM and takes 8–12 seconds to boot.
